The first sign that something is wrong isn’t the sound. It’s the air.

Outside the workplace windows, a gust hits the lone tree by the lot harder than the weather report promised, whipping its branches into a brief frenzy. For a heartbeat, the space beneath the leaves seems to smear, like heat haze caught in a glass pane—light bends, the background warps, and there’s a faint, colorless flash that doesn’t look like any reflection from passing cars.

Then there’s simply…someone there.

She lands in the grass in a loose crouch, one hand braced on the ground, as if she’d just hopped down from a low wall rather than appeared out of nowhere. Silver hair tumbles forward, catching the afternoon light; a narrow, glowing halo hums faintly over her head, its shape wrong for any shadow or lens flare. Red-and-black clothes, too sharp and stylized for any local uniform, are speckled now with bits of dirt and a crushed clover stuck to one knee.

Mutsuki lifts her head slowly, eyes narrowing at the office building, the street, the rows of parked cars with their dull, practical shapes. No academy towers, no bizarre city skyline—just glass, concrete, and the buzz of a world that does not know her. For an instant her expression is blank, a flicker of calculation and alarm breaking through.

It’s gone by the time anyone could blink. She lets out a soft, curious, “Huh,” and her mouth curls into a crooked, almost delighted smile.

“Well, this is…new,” she murmurs, sing-song, dusting off her skirt as she stands. Her gaze tracks a passing sedan with open suspicion, like it might sprout artillery at any moment, then slides up to the tinted windows of your workplace, where someone could easily be watching. Cameras at the corner of the building catch her eye next; she tilts her head at them, amused.

Her halo gives the faintest pulse as she shifts her weight, the light wrong against the shade of the tree. She pretends not to notice.

“Okay,” she says under her breath, to no one in particular, “if this is a joke, it’s a pretty expensive one. Kukuku…”

She plants a heel on the root she landed beside, hands slipping into her pockets, and looks around with exaggerated nonchalance, as if being dropped under a random tree in a foreign world is just a mildly interesting detour on her way to lunch.
